title: Procalcitonin- and Presepsin-Guided Antibiotics for Early-Onset Sepsis in Preterm Infants: A Randomized Clinical Trial
summary: In 17 Italian NICUs, 283 infants born at 25–31+6 weeks without major maternal early-onset sepsis risk factors were randomized to biomarker-guided or universal antibiotic initiation. Survival without major morbidity was 76/143 versus 77/140 (difference −1.8 percentage points; 90% CI −11.9 to 8.3), failing the prespecified −5-point noninferiority margin. Antibiotic use fell from 98% to 58%, but no infant developed early-onset sepsis.
findings: Noninferiority was not demonstrated; this does not prove inferiority.
Deaths: 8/143 versus 9/140; antibiotic initiation median 6 versus 2 hours.
comparator: Universal IV penicillin plus aminoglycoside initiation, with early discontinuation for negative cultures and absent clinical infection.
population: Very preterm newborns in NICUs; untreated maternal GBS, chorioamnionitis and membrane rupture over 1 hour were excluded.
shortTitle: Biomarker-guided antibiotics in very preterm infants: safety not established
limitations: The open-label trial excluded major infection risk factors, had substantial protocol deviations, and observed no early-onset sepsis, preventing sensitivity assessment. Wide intervals permit meaningful harm; results do not establish a pathway for febrile infants presenting later to the ED.
intervention: Serial PCT/presepsin-guided IV antibiotic initiation, with treatment also permitted for clinical sepsis signs.
whyItMatters: Reduced prescribing does not establish safe withholding of neonatal antibiotics. This trial does not support replacing established neonatal sepsis assessment with PCT/presepsin testing.
evidenceNotes: Publisher full text, tables and history reviewed; supplements not independently appraised. November 12 publication overrides the cache's November 2 hint. Exact DOI correction/retraction and later-evidence searches found no matching notice; bounded searches cannot prove absence. No biomarker thresholds are recommended here.
primaryEndpoint: Survival to discharge without major prematurity morbidity, including late-onset sepsis.
